title: The initiative
line: Threats that leave your opponent no time, and when time is worth a pawn.

steps.text: Time can be worth pawns. In the Danish Gambit, White gives pawns away to bring its pieces out fast.
Offer a pawn: push the pawn on c2 one square.
Offer a second pawn. Instead of taking back, bring your bishop out toward Black's king.
steps.after: Black takes again, and its pawn attacks your rook and bishop.

steps.text: Take the pawn with your other bishop.
steps.after: Two pawns down, but both bishops are out and aim at Black's king side.

steps.text: Black's queen came out early. Each threat against it costs Black a move while you bring out a piece. That is the initiative.
Bring out a knight that attacks the queen.

also.g1f3: That is fine too, but it makes no threat. This lesson attacks the queen to gain a move.

steps.after: The queen has to move again.

steps.text: Take the center while the queen is away: push the pawn in front of your queen two squares.

also.g1f3: That is as strong. This lesson takes the center first.

steps.after: Black gives its queen a way back.

steps.text: Both sides brought out a bishop. Now bring out your last one: it lines up with Black's queen, behind your knight.
steps.after: Black opens a road for its other bishop.

steps.text: Move the knight with a threat: it jumps to the center and uncovers your bishop's attack on the queen.

also.c3e4: That uncovers the attack too. This lesson goes on with the knight in the center.

steps.after: The queen goes back home. White has four pieces out, Black two.

summary: Make threats as you bring your pieces out. Each one costs your opponent a move, and time can be worth a pawn.
